title: Joining Forces: Brands And Vendors Making 3D Digital Transformation Easier
description:
A True End-to-End Process: How Brands & Vendors Can Achieve Co-Creation. The CLO team collaborates with global stakeholders across design, production, and market launch, we can identify the opportunities for brands and vendors when working together to overcome challenges and enhance the value of their existing digital assets. This video explores the workflow, as well as the roles and responsibilities of both brands and vendors.

Shirley Chan, 3D Design & Implementation Lead at CLO Hong Kong, presents the roles of vendors in 3D digitization, illustrating how brands and vendors can collaborate for easier adoption by highlighting best practices from clients and how the global CLO offices can support on this journey. 

As Blanca Olavarria, Marks and Spencer said, "The more the brands communicates the commitment and vision, the easier it is for the vendor to enter the journey with us and make the investment."

---

Everyone works together in the whole digital transformation journey. 3D is important. 3D is the core of the brands as the digital transformation. So we believe that brands should not be the only one in this 3D digital journey. Feed and production data of the 3D file are contained but not carried to the fitting, sampling and production stages. Here is an example of how the 3D digital end-to-end development can work with the vendors. When a brand starts with a new season, then the design team may need to do some strength research. Then they can use the closet visual board to create the trend board. Or they can make use of the data analysis function in closet to review the last season design, like which one is the most popular, which color is the best seller to the consumers. We can talk about sustainability or being efficient without clothes. Meanwhile, if you work with the ODM, actually these vendors can share this trend board in the same platform, which is closet, with you. Then the designers can co-create this visual board together with the vendors. For example, they can directly modify this visual ball later, to make it into a more customized one. And the vendor will understand more about what is your final design direction. And this vendor can also base on these updated direction to create more 3D designs and present more materials in the Virtual Showroom in closet. And once the direction is confirmed, then if you like the design style, you can proposed by your vendors then the designer can actually also comment and modify the outline maybe some small details in their file as well or let the vendors to create or modify it for you. You can work with your vendors who will give you the pattern blocks, trims and fabrics to provide you the digital format of these assets as well. So when these all materials are ready then the designers can overcome these challenges and not limited their creativity because of no materials to help them. On the brand side I think it's very important that we are super transparent with our vendors. It's not only about like the quality that we need of the 3Ds or which like workflows or type of files we need out of them to protect the quality of the 3D garment but more importantly is really like to communicate our vision so they understand our roadmap so I would say that's it. understand the commitment that we have because for them the role is really a lot of investment. It's investment in the right equipment, the right software, the right talent which is really difficult to find and nurture. We don't need to wait to have a physical sample in order to do the promotion and meanwhile the vendors can also reuse the assets that they create, consolidate the files that they have created to present their capacity to more business opportunities. For example, they can create an e-lookbook and then to do some outbound sales speech. You can also use these digital files in your e-commerce website. Then you can predict how the consumer likes your products. The more the brand communicates their commitment and their vision, the easier it is for the vendors to come in that journey for us. markdown_content: ## Collaborative 3D Digital Transformation in the Fashion Supply Chain This section explains the importance of collaboration between brands and vendors in the 3D digital transformation journey, focusing on digital supply chain integration, co-creation, and shared platforms. Brands and vendors working together enhance the benefits across the digital supply chain, particularly in 3D digital transformation, which is central to modern brand development. The collaboration ensures that 3D data—including feed and production data—is not only created but effectively carried through fitting, sampling, and production stages. For example, when a brand begins a new season, the design team conducts trend research using tools like Closet, a platform that supports creating visual trend boards and data analysis. Designers can review last season’s best-selling products and colors to inform new designs, promoting sustainability and efficiency by reducing unnecessary sampling. If working with Original Design Manufacturers (ODMs), the vendor can access the same trend board on Closet, enabling co-creation. Designers and vendors collaboratively modify the visual board to customize it, ensuring the vendor understands the brand’s final design direction. Vendors then create 3D designs and present materials in the Virtual Showroom on the same platform. Once the design direction is confirmed, designers can comment on or further modify outlines, or delegate modifications to vendors. Vendors provide digital assets such as pattern blocks, trims, and fabrics, which helps designers overcome material availability challenges and supports creative freedom. ## Transparency and Communication in Vendor Partnerships This section covers the necessity of transparent communication about quality standards, workflows, technical requirements, and long-term vision between brands and vendors to ensure successful 3D digital transformation. On the brand side, transparency with vendors is crucial—not only regarding 3D quality standards, file formats, and workflows but also about communicating the brand’s vision and roadmap. This clarity helps vendors understand the brand’s strategic commitment and justifies their investment in specialized equipment, software, and skilled talent, which are difficult to acquire and develop. Effective communication accelerates vendors’ willingness to invest in the right tools and processes, aligning their capabilities with the brand's digital transformation goals. ## Benefits of 3D Digital Assets for Brands and Vendors This section details the operational and commercial advantages of 3D digital assets, including reduced reliance on physical samples, enhanced promotional opportunities, and expanded sales channels. Brands no longer need to wait for physical samples to begin promotions, saving time and cost. Vendors can reuse and consolidate digital assets they create, showcasing their capacity to potential clients and opening new business opportunities. For instance, vendors can develop e-lookbooks using 3D digital files to support outbound sales efforts. Brands can also deploy these digital assets on e-commerce platforms, enabling predictive analytics on consumer preferences. The more brands communicate their commitment and vision, the easier it becomes for vendors to invest and participate fully in the digital transformation journey, creating a mutually beneficial ecosystem.
